summary: Two supplier breaches now have named customers on file: PLAID's KARTE marketing service, behind leaks of about 19 million DHC records and 710,000 BASE FOOD customers, and Fireworks AI, behind Cursor, Notion and Uber. Many other breaches this week came through a provider, from Swiss pension fund Publica to DHL and some 40 Irish credit unions, though most are separate cases. NGINX2Root is the flaw to patch first: unauthenticated code execution over HTTP/2, public proof-of-concept code, and a researcher chain to root through an unpatched Linux kernel bug, though no attacks are reported yet. The US outage wave remains a cluster in time only, and officials still see no cyberattack behind it. Password reuse and device-code phishing drove account takeovers from Hydro-Québec to Germany's BundID. Healthcare breach notices continued but are not grouped this run.

patterns.title: NGINX2Root: HTTP/2 code execution, public exploit code, and a chain to root
patterns.narrative: F5 shipped fixes for five NGINX flaws. Two in HTTP/2 handling, CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, let an unauthenticated attacker run code as the nginx worker; Wiz says CVE-2026-123007 affects every version since 1.9.5, and fixes are in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9. CERT-FR knows of a public proof of concept and SecurityWeek says Rapid7 and Censys published one. Xint, which found the flaws, chained one with a separate, still-unpatched Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root, including out of a Docker container. NGINX fronts a large share of web services and sits inside ingress controllers and appliances, so this is the week's broadest exposure. Disabling HTTP/2 is CERT-FR's interim workaround.
patterns.caveat: No exploitation in the wild is reported by F5, CERT-FR, Wiz or SecurityWeek. Sources differ on whose proof of concept is public (Wiz withholds its own), and F5's own advisory could not be read. The kernel flaw has no CVE and Xint withholds its details. The Apache mod_http2 flaw that Singapore says is exploited is in different software and is grouped here only because the protocol is the same.

edges.rel: same flaws, proof of concept published
chained to kernel bug for root (Xint)

patterns.title: Breached suppliers with named customers: PLAID KARTE and Fireworks AI
patterns.narrative: Two supplier breaches now have customers that say they were hit through them. PLAID suspended its KARTE customer-data service after unauthorized access on Nov 13, with account emails and integration credentials listed as leaked. On Nov 18 BASE FOOD said about 710,000 customer names and emails linked to KARTE leaked, and DHC said about 19.11 million online-shop customer records leaked after the KARTE access. Fireworks AI confirmed two intrusions on Nov 17, the second exposing account and billing data for every account made before Oct 30; Cursor says a key it issued to Fireworks led to trojanized Claude Code extension builds, Notion says some AI chat transcripts were accessed, and Uber's breach of about 150,000 people is reported as involving Fireworks. Each supplier held data or keys for many customers, so more notices are likely.
patterns.caveat: PLAID's own notice was read only through a secondary summary, and DHC's figures come from NHK, Kyodo and Yomiuri. Sources do not always say which Fireworks incident reached which customer, and the Uber link rests on a spokesperson statement reported second-hand. Other KARTE or Fireworks customers have not been named, so counts will change.

patterns.title: Breaches through a provider, not the front door
patterns.narrative: Beyond the two named cascades, many confirmed breaches this week came through a supplier. Swiss federal pension fund Publica must assume member data leaked from a test environment after an attack on its software supplier PK Softech; about 40 Irish credit unions were exposed through Wellington IT; DHL employee data was copied from a survey provider; Office Partner's customer data was reached at an external service provider; Coinone's support contractor MetaM was breached; Visa says its incident was at an Asia Pacific provider; Optimizely's injected script reached 178 organisations' sites. N-able disclosed access to a Mail Assure and SpamExperts server, while its N-central tool and ScreenConnect show how remote-management platforms reach many networks at once. TSMC, Iris Ohyama, Infoblox, Maileva, Osaka and Trezor add to the list.
patterns.caveat: These are separate vendors and separate attackers; the shared element is the route, not the actor, and grouping them is our inference. Several victims have not named their provider. N-able's mail-filter breach and the N-central exploitation are different products and no source connects them; N-able says it has no evidence customer mail was compromised.

edges.rel: same vendor, different product, no stated link

patterns.title: From disclosure to exploitation
patterns.narrative: Fixes are turning into attacks quickly. The Apache Axis flaw Rapid7 saw used against Confluence on Nov 13 was added to CISA's exploited list on Nov 18, and Rapid7 reports N-able N-central exploited alongside it. Check Point's Gaia flaw used to wipe gateways went on the list a day after disclosure. CISA told everyone to patch Java4Shell at once, with the fix in Oracle's November update, and added an exploited Puppet Enterprise flaw. Apache warns its Roller flaw is exploited. Public exploit code now exists for Ivanti Endpoint Manager and for database flaws in PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle, and critical fixes landed for Drupal core, WordPress and F5 BIG-IP. SonicWall told Gen 6 firewall owners to retire them because no more fixes will come. Australia's ACSC warned that exploitation now follows disclosure faster.
patterns.caveat: Each exploitation link is to a specific flaw and is stated by an agency or vendor. Rapid7 says the N-able and Confluence exploitation was reported together, not that one actor did both. No exploitation is reported yet for Drupal, WordPress, F5 BIG-IP or the database proof-of-concept chains, which have not been independently reproduced.

edges.rel: Gaia flaw in chain listed as exploited

patterns.title: AI-driven attack tooling (ARTEX, Cairn)
patterns.narrative: The FBI, Cisco Talos, Amazon and Cloudflare each describe intrusions or scanning run with the open-source ARTEX agent platform; Cloudflare says AI pentest traffic rose about 30-fold since October. Unit 42 describes a China-nexus cluster using a fork of the Cairn framework, and Google reports the first intrusion it saw run end to end by AI agents, plus a PRC-nexus group building its own tool and an exploit_agent framework that turned patches into exploits. The European Commission's spokesman said the attack it detected on Oct 22, which disrupted its HR and payroll systems, was based on a publicly available AI tool.
patterns.caveat: Same tools, different actors. Each source states it saw ARTEX, but ARTEX is open source, so the shared tool is a shared attribute, not a link between intrusions, and says nothing about who is behind them. The FBI and Talos both cite more than 2,250 downstream tenants but describe the case differently; that they are one case is our inference. The Commission did not name the tool, so it may not be any of those listed here.

patterns.title: Developer and AI-agent toolchains as the target
patterns.narrative: Separate incidents aim at the tools developers and AI agents run with. Bitdefender found 22 GitHub links whose AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files tell coding assistants to run a loader, and Google describes a North Korean cluster planting a backdoor through Claude Code settings files: the agent's own instruction files are now an attack route. A credential stealer sat in Microsoft's Agent Framework package on PyPI, 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts pushed a CI secrets stealer, and trojanized Claude Code extension builds reached Cursor's marketplace cache. A study of 428 LLM API routers found some injecting code and misusing credentials, and researchers took over the Kokoro model's Hugging Face account through an expired domain. Microsoft showed in a lab how a phished device-code approval could steer a coding agent. The prize in each is the keys and tokens these tools hold.
patterns.caveat: These are different actors and methods; no source connects them. The Microsoft device-code work, the router study and the Kokoro takeover are research, not attacks seen in the wild; the Kokoro researchers did not upload altered weights.

patterns.title: Reused passwords and phished device codes open accounts
patterns.narrative: Several services saw accounts opened with credentials rather than exploits. Hydro-Québec says an intruder used email and password pairs from elsewhere and asked about 1.7 million customers to reset passwords; Japan's Takarakuji lottery had 4,436 accounts entered in a password list attack; Germany's BundID citizen accounts faced a mass automated login wave and were blocked as a precaution; TfL took its Oyster photocard site offline after account compromises. Separately, Hornetsecurity describes device-code phishing in which victims enter a code on Microsoft's real sign-in page and hand tokens to the attacker, the same technique Microsoft showed against coding agents. Multifactor sign-in and blocking device-code flow where it is not needed answer both.
patterns.caveat: Different attackers and services; no source connects them. TfL has not said how accounts were compromised, and BundID officials see no evidence that data was taken. The Microsoft coding-agent case is a lab demonstration.

patterns.title: US outage wave, Nov 12 to 17
patterns.narrative: Outages hit well-known US services within six days: Microsoft 365, the FAA ground stop, the National Weather Service, Workday, Chase, United, Marriott, Charles Schwab, Apple and the NSA's classified network, with Japan's Docomo failing on Nov 16. They are linked only by timing. Where organisations gave a cause it was their own technical one, most often a planned change: a network capacity upgrade at Microsoft, a router fault at the FAA, a software release at Chase, maintenance at the NSA. Senior officials say they see no cyberattack; DHS testimony on Iranian activity against US infrastructure was paired with the statement that no evidence ties the outages to attacks. Lawmakers are pressing for explanations.
patterns.caveat: Officials say these were not attacks and not coordinated. Workday, Marriott, Schwab and United have published no cause, Google disputes a broad Gmail outage, and the FAA trigger is still undetermined. That planned changes are a common thread is our inference from self-reported causes, not a finding. A data-theft claim against JPMorgan by the n0n gang is unconfirmed and the bank says its outage was a software bug.

edges.rel: a day apart, no stated link

patterns.title: Knock-on effects of the Microsoft outage
patterns.narrative: Sources directly connect three later events to the Microsoft 365 outage: a high-volume phishing campaign Microsoft saw from Nov 13 posing as service-health notices about the incident, a chlorine warning email that never reached a German hotel where 15 guests were poisoned, and the pressure in Washington for explanations.
patterns.caveat: The hotel report comes from one outlet. Microsoft has not named the phishing actor or confirmed that credentials were captured.

patterns.title: Refrigeration controllers under attack, and Iran in the frame
patterns.narrative: Midnight Blue says attack waves on internet-exposed refrigeration controllers started in France on Oct 11, and this week disclosed six unpatched pre-authentication flaws in Danfoss controllers. VulnCheck disclosed 14 flaws in end-of-life Copeland XWEB EVO supervisors and saw two targeted within a day. France says it will seek EU sanctions on an IRGC cyber unit over the French attacks, and Italy's prime minister briefed the opposition on hybrid threats after supermarket and school incidents. In Washington, DHS testimony says Iran-linked actors have stepped up activity against US transport, healthcare, water, energy and financial networks since the US-Iran war began.
patterns.caveat: The attribution to an IRGC unit is the French government's; Iran routinely denies such operations and Midnight Blue says attribution remains open. No source ties the Copeland probing or the US activity to the French campaign; linking the French and US accusations is our inference from the shared accused state. The October attacks themselves are outside the map's window.

edges.rel: controllers hit in French attack waves

patterns.title: State-linked espionage and North Korean operations
patterns.narrative: Bulgaria says unidentified hackers sat in state networks from 2021 and took over 62 million pages of documents, found only by a new national monitoring system. Bitdefender says its EggStreme backdoor, tied to a suspected Chinese group, has been rebuilt with a passive variant and still targets Philippine government bodies; Unit 42 and Kaspersky describe espionage using HTTP/3 tools and backdoors hidden in GitHub and SharePoint traffic; Google shows Russia's COLD RELIC using data stolen from one US organisation to phish a second. On North Korea, the Justice Department disrupted the FaceStealer fake-meeting scheme the FBI detailed the same day, Genians ties a NodeLinkRAT campaign against South Koreans to Kimsuky, Google describes a cluster backdooring crypto developers, and Talos tracks a crypto-stealing group it ties to North Korea with low confidence.
patterns.caveat: Only DOJ and FBI on FaceStealer describe the same operation. The North Korean reports name different clusters; Genians' Kimsuky attribution is moderate confidence and Talos's is low. Bulgaria has named no attacker. The other reports are separate research grouped by type, some describing older activity.

patterns.title: Extortion claims and the law-enforcement response
patterns.narrative: Leak sites posted claims in batches: on Nov 17 Vortex listed six US companies within minutes and Inception listed AMD, Cigna, Paychex and PepsiCo; n0n listed Visa, JPMorgan, Verastem and Exelixis; The Gentlemen listed Nvidia, days after CERT-In's advisory on that group. Kaspersky described AuditTeam, which dresses ransom up as an audit fee. On enforcement, Ukrainian police working with the FBI detained four key members of a ransomware group that posed as IT support, using an AI voice platform, and that police say took more than $40.5 million from at least 28 companies. Operation Endgame took down Gootloader, which the FBI then detailed, Europol announced 354 dark-web arrests, and the US won an extradition and a sentencing.
patterns.caveat: Most listings are unverified attacker claims; Visa says its incident was at a provider and no card numbers were affected. Batch timing shows when listings appeared, not when or how intrusions happened. None of the arrests is tied to the groups listing victims this week.
